judge_assessment.explanation: Every rate the judge claims to have divided checks out: (1/2)/(1/4) = 2, (3/4)/(1/2) = 3/2, (2/3)/(1/6) = 4, (3/2)/(3/4) = 2, Rowan (3/5)/(1/4) = 12/5 against Sadie (2/3)/(1/3) = 2 so '>', (5/8)/(5/6) = 3/4, (7/8)/(1/2) = 7/4, 6/(3/4) = 8, (2/5)/(3/4) = 8/15, Brand A 2/(2/3) = 3 against Brand B 3/(3/4) = 4 so '<', (9/2)/(3/4) = 6, and the two-step bottler (9/4)/(1/3) = 27/4 scaled by 4 = 27. This is also the only sheet in my batch where printed response slots and verify entries match exactly: problems 5 and 10 each print two rate blanks plus a relation blank and each carries three entries. The one thing the judge's answer_key_quality 4 passes over is the Quick Answers bank, which prints '5. 12/5, 2, --' and '10. 3, 4, --'. Both dashes are the verified relations, and this sheet declares no manual items, so the reserved glyph is being used for checks that passed.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 5 and 10 are the coverage model the rest of this batch should follow: the worksheet prints three response slots each (Rowan, Sadie and the relation; Brand A, Brand B and the relation) and verify.json carries exactly three entries per id, including the relation as a `compare` on the original fractional expressions rather than on rounded decimals.

Every expected value is an exact rational -- '3/2', '12/5', '3/4', '7/4', '8/15' -- so a key that silently rounded 8/15 to 0.53 could not pass. On a fractional-unit-rate sheet that is the difference between checking the skill and checking a decimal approximation of it.

Problem 12 is a genuine two-step: find (2 1/4)/(1/3) = 6.75 litres per minute and only then scale to 4 minutes for 27, with the declared trap (2 1/4)*4 = 9 for the student who treats the given amount as if it were already the rate. The trap value is far enough from 27 that the error cannot hide.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt() sympifies string expecteds and falls back to '---' when that raises, so the '>' in problem 5 and the '<' in problem 10 are replaced by the glyph the module reserves for manual-only items -- on a sheet that has no manual items at all.
evidence: verify.json id 5 compare ['(3/5)/(1/4)','(2/3)/(1/3)'] expected '>' and id 10 compare ['2/(2/3)','3/(3/4)'] expected '<', both passing (16 checks, gate chain green)
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 56-61 return '---' on SympifyError; lines 71-73 return the same '---' for a manual-only id
final_response.md correctly states 'The two comparisons were checked as relations', which the delivered bank then hides

improvements.title: Render the verified relations in problems 5 and 10 instead of an em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: Teach the Quick Answers bank to render a verified relation. In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, render_entry() should special-case an entry whose type is 'compare' with order 'relation': build the line from the entry's own `values` and `expected`, e.g. `$34 < 34.2$`, instead of handing the bare string '<' to _fmt(). _fmt() must stop returning '---' for a relation token, and '---' must remain reserved for items that carry no `expected` at all (genuine manual review), so the two states are visually distinct on the page.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py gains this case's id 5: entries [eval '12/5', eval 2, compare ['(3/5)/(1/4)','(2/3)/(1/3)'] expected '>']. Assert the rendered line ends with a typeset '>' relation and contains no '---'; additionally assert that a bank generated from a verify.json with zero manual entries contains no '---' anywhere. render_entry returns '12/5, 2, ---' today, so both assertions fail before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The last two blanks on an otherwise fully covered key disappear, and the 'no manual entries implies no dashes' invariant becomes testable for every future sheet.
improvements.risk: Low. One formatting function; the only real risk is LaTeX escaping when a relation is typeset beside fractions such as 12/5, which the test covers by compiling the fixture key.

case_summary: The cleanest case in my batch. Twelve fractional unit-rate problems, all recomputed here and correct, expecteds kept as exact rationals so a rounded key could not pass, comparisons verified as relations on the original fractional expressions, and -- uniquely in this batch -- printed response slots that match verify entries one for one on the two multi-answer problems. No open-response prompts exist, so nothing needed a manual flag and the claim that nothing was left for a human is true. The single defect is the delivered Quick Answers bank, which prints '--' for the two verified relations, using the glyph reserved for unchecked items on a sheet with no unchecked items. Minor delivery note: unlike eight of its siblings, final_response.md names the three documents by role without printing their filenames -- all three artifacts are still surfaced, so this is a consistency wart rather than the artifact-surfacing failure.
